title: Usage-envelope protocol and statistical reconciliation for at-least-once metering
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: At-scale customers using aggressive client-side retries and edge proxies continue to produce transient duplicate ingestion that we bill for, or that inflates quota usage and trips hard rate limits. Existing per-request seals and long-lived session leases are either too heavyweight for bursty mobile clients or too stateful for our edge fleet.

Goal: Design and implement a light-weight, high-throughput metering protocol that prevents double-charging in the common retry patterns while keeping server-side state small and allowing eventual reconciliation for rare duplicate windows. The approach should integrate with existing quota enforcement and the accounting pipeline so that billing and console metrics remain accurate without adding visible latency to request paths.
proposal_summary: Introduce a client-side "usage envelope" signed by the client SDK with a compact monotonic envelope-id and a short-lived escrow token. Servers will accept envelopes optimistically (fast path) and attach a provisional commit mark to the customer ledger. A background reconciliation pipeline uses probabilistic duplicate detection (Bloom-resident sliding window) combined with end-of-day exact reconciliation to correct rare overcharges. UX: clients get immediate provisional receipts; final receipts after reconciliation if charges changed. Falls back to strict server-side commit for high-value requests.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional receipts issued in <= 10ms additional latency on the critical path for 95th percentile
Duplicate charge rate under standard test traffic <= 0.05% before reconciliation
Reconciliation pipeline reduces any remaining duplicate overcharge to 0 and annotates customer billing events with correction metadata
Integration tests demonstrating correct behavior when client replays envelope with same monotonic id across multiple edge pods
Console shows provisional vs final charge delta in per-customer billing UI and exportable report
design_decisions: Use client monotonic envelope-id (32-bit) + client epoch to keep envelope size minimal
Short-lived escrow token (TTL ~30s) held by edge nodes to validate optimistic commits; escrow implemented as consistent hash shards to avoid global locking
Bloom slide window for low-memory in-flight duplicate detection; false positives handled by reconciliation corrections rather than blocking the fast path
Separate code paths for 'standard' requests (optimistic) and 'high-value' requests (synchronous commit) configurable by product quota tiers
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from Bloom filter may lead to unnecessary reconciliation work — mitigation: tune filter size per-customer and use adaptive windowing based on traffic profile

Clock skew on clients may cause monotonic ids to reset — mitigation: include client epoch and require server-side monotonic advancement heuristics; fallback to server-assigned id when epoch mismatch detected
Edge pod crashes could lose short-lived escrow state — mitigation: escrow is replicated to N=3 via quorum writes; reconciliation corrects any transient inconsistencies

Customer confusion over provisional vs final billing — mitigation: Console UI and billing exports will clearly label provisional charges and show reconciliation corrections; notify customers for corrections > $X
implementation_plan: 1) Spec: finalize envelope format and escrow API (Confluence doc) — owner: Priya (3d)
2) SDK changes: add envelope generator + optimistic-send logic to Node/Python SDKs (Diego, 5d)
3) Edge runtime: accept provisional envelopes, attach provisional_commit metadata and forward to accounting pipeline (Edge team, 7d)
4) Bloom window service: implement per-customer sliding Bloom filter cache in accounting front (Infra, 5d)
5) Reconciliation pipeline: map provisional commits to actual ingestion and emit correction entries (Billing, 10d)
6) Console: show provisional vs final and export reconciliation reports (Product/Console, 6d)
7) E2E tests & load tests: simulate common retry patterns and mobile bursts (SRE, 4d)
8) Phased rollout: opt-in alpha customers -> beta -> default with release notes and anonymized correction telemetry (2w)
9) Post-launch: run 30-day monitoring and tune parameters (sizing, bloom fp rate)
open_questions: What threshold defines 'high-value' where we require synchronous commits? (billing team input)
Should provisional charges count against soft quotas immediately or only against burst buckets?
What is the maximum acceptable false positive correction rate from a legal/billing perspective?
How to expose reconciliation delay SLAs to customers (e.g., 'finalized within 24h')

notes: This ticket is intentionally designed to reduce per-request state on edges while retaining strong eventual correctness for billing.
The reconciliation pipeline is where we accept complexity: fast path remains simple and low-latency; heavy work is batched offline and credited back as needed.
If this design proves too noisy for high-frequency low-dollar customers, we will gate optimistic commits by customer tier and default to synchronous commit for enterprise tenants.
